## File naming
issue 846

::: {.callout-note}
This is meant as a guideline, if your lab equipment produces data that does use spaces and special characters it is not always feasible to rename everything. Yoda will be able to store it properly, but be aware of the gotchas mentioned. 
:::

Yoda is capable of dealing with special characters and long file names, but to avoid problems when transferring your files to other systems it is good to follow some naming conventions for file and folder names:

- **Only use lowercase characters**
MacOS, irods and linux filesystems are case sensitive, but Windows is not, which can lead to unexpected behavior. 

- **Avoid special characters**

- **Avoid spaces, use `-` or `_`**
Accessing data from the CLI (Command Line Interface) or a script is a lot easier if you avoid spaces. Take editing `run 1/my data.json`. `vi run 1/my data.json` will not work and you need to remember to use quotes `vi "run 1/my data.json"` or "escape" `vi run\ 1/my\ data.json`, while the path `run1/my_data.json` is just as clearly readable, but easier to access: `vi run1/my_data.json`. 

- **Try to keep file and folder names as short as possible**
Windows for example has a maximum path (folder, subfolders and file) length of 250 characters. You could for example upload a file 100 subfolders deep from a Linux system (such as ADA or Snellius) and find you are unable to download it to your Windows laptop.
